rows.title: Best of 2019: DOT says transportation capital program needs more funding
rows.standfirst: DOT officials say Connecticut needs to increase capital spending by 30 percent to transform the state’s aging, overcrowded transportation system.

rows.title: State can’t rely on raising hospital taxes to survive next recession
rows.standfirst: Connecticut relied on nearly $2 billion from hospitals to help the state crawl out of the last recession. It won’t have that money when the next recession hits.

rows.title: New laws affect parking, dry cleaning, eye doctor visits
rows.standfirst: More than two dozen new state laws went into effect on Jan. 1, ranging from expanded health insurance coverage and paid leave to changes in court, property and DMV rules.

rows.title: Lamont eyes emergency budget cuts, even as reserves swell
rows.standfirst: Gov. Ned Lamont recently raised the specter of emergency budget cuts, which typically hit nonprofits and higher education the hardest.

rows.title: Nonprofits ‘greatly concerned’ about prospect of emergency budget cuts
rows.standfirst: Nonprofit agencies urged Gov. Ned Lamont’s administration to steer clear of community-based social services as it seeks to close a small hole in state finances.

rows.title: A crucial day for Lamont’s transportation ambitions
rows.standfirst: The prospects for passing a truck tolls transportation plan should be evident today after a Senate Democratic caucus.

rows.title: Senate Democrats near ‘contingent consensus’ on truck tolls
rows.standfirst: The Democratic majorities of the General Assembly edged ever so cautiously Tuesday toward a consensus on a 10-year, $19 billion transportation infrastructure plan.

rows.title: Fed projects economic slip for CT in first half of 2020
rows.standfirst: New projections from the Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia list Connecticut as one of nine states likely to face economic contraction during the first half of 2020.

rows.title: Lamont says he has ‘resolved’ transportation issues with Senate
rows.standfirst: The goal is to pass the $19 billion transportation bill, which requires tolls for tractor trailers, before the regular 2020 session opens Feb. 5.

rows.title: Business-owning lawmakers spar over state employees, economic climate
rows.standfirst: Lawmakers who participated in an annual economic summit Monday differed on whether CT is becoming more friendly or hostile to businesses.

rows.title: State OT costs continue to creep up, but salary expenses remain way down
rows.standfirst: State agency overtime expenses continue to rise, according to a new report, but overall salary costs remain below those of a decade ago.

rows.title: CT Voices proposes major state tax shift to reverse inequality
rows.standfirst: A leading child advocacy group challenged state leaders Wednesday to reverse escalating income and wealth inequality and provide tax relief for poor and middle-income households by shifting tax burdens onto the state’s millionaires.

rows.title: New report shows state revenue has remained stable
rows.standfirst: The latest revenue projections show CT can expect $169 million more than the governor and legislators originally anticipated.

rows.title: CT’s unpaid legislator wants to champion push for lawmaker pay reform
rows.standfirst: Sen. Norm Needleman, who does not accept compensation from the state, wants to end nearly two decades of no pay raises for lawmakers.

rows.title: Lamont’s property tax relief pledge comes due in February
rows.standfirst: To keep his 2018 campaign pledge, Lamont must deliver $375 million in property tax relief. That isn’t looking likely.

rows.title: Senate Dems say election year shouldn’t stymie pot debate
rows.standfirst: Though Connecticut legislators tend to shy away from controversial issues during re-election years, Senate Democrats insisted Thursday that legalization of recreational marijuana use still could be enacted this year if bundled with social justice components.

rows.title: Churches, nonprofits win repeal of federal tax
rows.standfirst: Connecticut lawmakers backed efforts to repeal a 21% tax imposed on parking and transportation benefits for employees of churches and other nonprofits.

rows.title: Senate Democrats pledge to reverse federal funding cuts to Planned Parenthood
rows.standfirst: Senate Democrats pledged Friday to replenish federal funds the Trump administration has stripped from Planned Parenthood clinics in the region.

rows.title: Ten times promises to grow transportation funding were broken
rows.standfirst: Since 2007, lawmakers and governors have agreed 10 times to reduce previous commitments to transfer resources from the budget’s General Fund to the Special Transportation Fund.

rows.title: Broken promises to fund transportation defined last 15 years
rows.standfirst: Connecticut’s transportation program has been riddled for more than a decade by broken funding promises from both political parties.

rows.title: A deal on bonding and a drafted transportation bill move CT closer to tolls
rows.standfirst: Gov. Ned Lamont and the General Assembly took two significant steps closer to ordering electronic tolls on large trucks that travel Connecticut’s highways.

rows.title: ‘Right to Housing’ gains traction among top legislators heading into the session
rows.standfirst: ‘Right to Housing’ is a popular concept in Europe, but it’s yet to gain traction in the U.S.

rows.title: A tribe, a state and a mutual reliance on gambling
rows.standfirst: It’s unclear how permissive the Land of Steady Habits is willing to be in gambling’s new digital age. The secondary question is how much of the action will be handled by Connecticut’s tribal casinos.

rows.title: Fasano says tolls bill has loophole that could capture cars
rows.standfirst: The top Senate Republican charged Democrats Tuesday with building a “workaround” provision into the new truck tolls bill.

rows.title: An effort in Connecticut to end the economic border wars
rows.standfirst: Can the states agree to mutually disarm when it comes to the billions of dollars in economic incentives that are spent annually coaxing companies to move, expand or sometimes merely stay put?

rows.title: Sweeping gambling bill is meant to push Lamont
rows.standfirst: Democratic leaders endorsed legislation that would give the state’s two federally recognized tribes exclusive rights to take bets on sports, open a casino in Bridgeport and offer a broad array of virtual casino games on smart phones and computers.

rows.title: Lamont offers two new job incentive programs
rows.standfirst: Gov. Ned Lamont unveiled his first legislative proposals Wednesday for 2020: a new incentive program for businesses to expand or relocate jobs to Connecticut and a revised small business assistance initiative.

rows.title: Nonprofits reframe their big ask, seek a share of future budget windfalls
rows.standfirst: Rebuffed in their bid last year to capture $100 million of the state’s growing reserves, Connecticut’s nonprofit social service agencies now want a share of future projected budget surpluses.

rows.title: Democrats promise passage of truck tolls in two weeks
rows.standfirst: After cancelling a special session slated for Monday, Democratic legislative leaders assured Gov. Ned Lamont that they have the votes to pass his transportation funding plan the week of Feb. 10.
